header.title: Household
header.subtitle: Who is in the household, who owns each account, and how transactions are attributed to a person. Names stay on this machine.

members.title: Members
members.subtitle: Declared in memory/household.yaml. A model only ever sees adult-1, kid-1 ... never a name or an alias.
members.footer: Add or change members with coach memory member add or on the Memory page. Children's pocket money is on Kids' money.

accounts.title: Accounts: owner and purpose
accounts.subtitle: The owner is who the account belongs to (joint, or one member). It is the default for every transaction on it.

rules.title: Attribution rules
rules.subtitle: Who a transaction belongs to: a manual reassignment, then the first matching rule, then the account's owner.
rules.empty: No rule: the owner of the account decides. Typical rules: a prepaid card account per child, or a card's last four digits on a shared account.
rules.confirmRemove: Remove the rule "{{id}}"? It is recorded in the memory history.
rules.manual_one: {{count}} transaction reassigned by hand (open a transaction to change or undo one).
rules.manual_other: {{count}} transactions reassigned by hand (open a transaction to change or undo one).

ruleDialog.title: New attribution rule
ruleDialog.description: Every condition you fill must match (AND). The preview shows how many transactions it would attribute.
ruleDialog.cardHint: only when the bank prints them in the description
ruleDialog.preview_one: It matches {{count}} transaction; {{change}} would change person.
ruleDialog.preview_other: It matches {{count}} transactions; {{change}} would change person.

logins.title: Logins
logins.subtitle: Each person can have their own login: an adult sees everything, a child sees only their own money. Logins are created in a terminal, never here.
logins.empty: No login yet: the app opens with the owner's login (everything).

audit.title: Who changed what
audit.subtitle: The changes made in the web app (method, endpoint, who: never a payload) and the memory history with the source of each change.
audit.requests: Changes made in the web app

header.title: Who pays what
header.subtitle: Shared costs (house, cars, insurance) split by the rules you set. A cost paid from the joint account settles nothing; what a person paid from their own money is compared with their fair share.

empty.title: No allocation rule yet
empty.body: A rule says which costs it covers (a category, a group, a tag, a merchant), how they are shared (50/50, by income, custom percentages) and between whom.

total.title: All rules together
total.subtitle: Positive: the others owe this person. Negative: this person owes.

whoPays.footnote: A split of the past, computed by code from the transactions attributed to each person. It moves no money and is not legal or tax advice on a couple's finances.

dialog.title: New allocation rule
dialog.description: Shared between every adult unless you pick custom percentages. The first rule that matches a payment takes it.
